title: High Clinical Exome Sequencing Diagnostic Rates and Novel Phenotypic Expansions for Nonisolated Microphthalmia, Anophthalmia, and Coloboma.
authors: Kunisetty, Bhavana; Martin-Giacalone, Bailey A; Zhao, Xiaonan; Luna, Pamela N; Brooks, Brian P; Hufnagel, Robert B; Shaw, Chad A; Rosenfeld, Jill A; Agopian, A J; Lupo, Philip J; Scott, Daryl A
one_liner_zh: 该研究评估临床外显子测序在非孤立性小眼畸形等疾病中的诊断率，虽用机器学习算法但核心为临床诊断与表型扩展，无蛋白质-DNA互作或结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: PURPOSE: A molecular diagnosis is only made in a subset of individuals with nonisolated microphthalmia, anophthalmia, and coloboma (MAC). This may be due to underutilization of clinical (whole) exome sequencing (cES) and an incomplete understanding of the genes that cause MAC. The purpose of this study is to determine the efficacy of cES in cases of nonisolated MAC and to identify new MAC phenotypic expansions. METHODS: We determined the efficacy of cES in 189 individuals with nonisolated MAC. We then used cES data, a validated machine learning algorithm, and previously published expression data, case reports, and animal models to determine which candidate genes were most likely to contribute to the development of MAC. RESULTS: We found the efficacy of cES in nonisolated MAC to be between 32.3% (61/189) and 48.1% (91/189). Most genes affected in our cohort were not among genes currently screened in clinically available ophthalmologic gene panels. A subset of the genes implicated in our cohort had not been clearly associated with MAC. Our analyses revealed sufficient evidence to support low-penetrance MAC phenotypic expansions involving nine of these human disease genes. CONCLUSIONS: We conclude that cES is an effective means of identifying a molecular diagnosis in individuals with nonisolated MAC and may identify putatively damaging variants that would be missed if only a clinically available ophthalmologic gene panel was obtained. Our data also suggest that deleterious variants in BRCA2, BRIP1, KAT6A, KAT6B, NSF, RAC1, SMARCA4, SMC1A, and TUBA1A can contribute to the development of MAC.
abstract_zh: 目的：仅在部分非孤立性小眼球、无眼球和眼缺损（MAC）患者中实现分子诊断。这可能归因于临床（全）外显子组测序（cES）的利用不足以及对导致MAC的基因认识不全面。本研究旨在评估cES在非孤立性MAC病例中的诊断效能，并识别新的MAC表型扩展。方法：我们确定了189例非孤立性MAC个体中cES的诊断效能。随后，利用cES数据、经过验证的机器学习算法、已发表的表达数据、病例报告和动物模型，以判断哪些候选基因最可能参与MAC的发生发展。结果：我们发现cES在非孤立性MAC中的诊断效能介于32.3%（61/189）至48.1%（91/189）之间。我们队列中受影响的大多数基因并不在目前临床可用的眼科基因检测组合所筛查的基因之列。队列中涉及的部分基因此前尚未明确与MAC相关联。我们的分析提供了充分证据，支持涉及其中九个人类疾病基因的低外显率MAC表型扩展。结论：我们得出结论，cES是识别非孤立性MAC个体分子诊断的有效手段，并可能识别出仅通过临床可用眼科基因检测组合会遗漏的潜在有害变异。我们的数据还提示，BRCA2、BRIP1、KAT6A、KAT6B、NSF、RAC1、SMARCA4、SMC1A和TUBA1A中的有害变异可促进MAC的发生发展。
